```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import _pcpkg as P
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat

DOC = "PTP-001"
UO = None
UO_TITLE = "A-Mab Drug Substance"

# --- revision, investigation and dates (config campaign:) ------------------------------
ver, eff = doc_version(DOC)
appr_v1 = str(rev1_date(DOC))                   # Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on this date
pkg_date = str(REV1["effective"])               # the date the Version 1.0 title blocks carried
ra_appr, pcmp_appr = str(PLAN_APPROVAL["RA-001"]), str(PLAN_APPROVAL["PCMP-001"])
inv_id, inv2_id = INV["id"], INV2["id"]
inv_opened, inv_closed, inv_class = str(INV["opened"]), str(INV["closed"]), INV["classification"]
amd_id, amd_date = AMD["id"], str(AMD["date"])
assert DOC in CAPA.set_index("id").loc["CA3", "action"]     # corrective action CA3 reissues this plan
assert appr_v1 != pkg_date

# --- the studies recorded in the Version 1.0 reports, and when they ran ------------------
chron = csv("study_chronology.csv")
v1 = chron[chron["end"].astype(str) < pkg_date].copy()
n_v1 = len(v1)
first_start, last_end = str(v1["start"].min()), str(v1["end"].max())
first_study = v1.sort_values("start").iloc[0]["id"]
# this plan came before the risk basis, the master plan and every study
assert appr_v1 < ra_appr < pcmp_appr < first_start
assert last_end < pkg_date

steps = list(CFG.train_order)
def plan_of(k):
    return f"PCP-{CFG.unit_op(k).step:03d}"
def report_of(k):
    return f"PCR-{CFG.unit_op(k).step:03d}"

win_rows = []
for k in steps:
    g = v1[v1["step"] == k]
    pa = str(PLAN_APPROVAL[plan_of(k)])
    assert pa < str(g["start"].min())                       # each plan approved before its first study
    win_rows.append([CFG.unit_op(k).step, UNIT_OP_TITLES[k], plan_of(k), pa, len(g),
                     str(g["start"].min()), str(g["end"].max())])
win = pd.DataFrame(win_rows, columns=["Step", "Unit operation", "Plan", "Plan approved", "Studies",
                                      "First study start", "Last study end"])
assert int(win["Studies"].sum()) == n_v1
overlap = [(a[0], b[0]) for i, a in enumerate(win_rows) for b in win_rows[i + 1:]
           if not (a[6] < b[5] or b[6] < a[5])]
assert overlap                                               # some steps were studied in parallel

# --- package, product and process ------------------------------------------------------
n_docs = len(DOC_REGISTRY)
assert set(INVESTIGATIONS) <= set(DOC_REGISTRY)
meta = CFG.raw()["meta"]
scale_l, ds_conc, n_ppq = meta["commercial_scale_l"], meta["drug_substance_target_g_per_l"], meta["n_ppq_batches"]
n_steps = len(steps)
step_first, step_last = CFG.unit_op(steps[0]).step, CFG.unit_op(steps[-1]).step
s_har, s_ufdf = CFG.unit_op("harvest").step, CFG.unit_op("ufdf").step

train_rows = process_steps_df().values.tolist()

cqa_tab = all_cqas()
n_cqa = len(cqa_tab)
_reg = cqa_reg.set_index("key")
assert _reg.loc["fragments_lmw", "set_by"] == "harvest"     # the register assigns fragments to harvest
assert "nrCE-SDS" in _reg.loc["fragments_lmw", "unit"]
_cat_order = list(dict.fromkeys(cqa_tab["Category"]))
cqa_frame = (cqa_tab.assign(_o=cqa_tab["Category"].map(_cat_order.index))
             .sort_values("_o", kind="stable").drop(columns="_o"))
cqa_frame = cqa_frame[["Category", "CQA", "Acceptance", "Criticality", "Tool #1"]].copy()
cqa_frame["Category"] = cqa_frame["Category"].str.capitalize()
tbl_cqa = T.frame(
    cqa_frame, "Drug substance quality attributes, acceptance criteria and assigned criticality.",
    "tbl-cqa", merge=["Category"], align=["P{2.6cm}", "P{4.8cm}", "P{3.8cm}", "c", "r"],
    notes=[("", "VL, very low. L, low. M, moderate. H, high. VH, very high. A level such as M-H lies "
                "between the two levels it names. Tool #1, the criticality score of the case study, the "
                "product of impact and uncertainty.")])

# --- characterization scope and classification ------------------------------------------
scope = char_scope_df()
n_par, n_mv, n_uv = int(scope["Parameters"].sum()), int(scope["Multivariate"].sum()), int(scope["Univariate"].sum())
nodoe_steps = set(scope.loc[scope["Multivariate"] == 0, "Step"])
assert nodoe_steps == {s_har, s_ufdf}                       # harvest and UF/DF carry no designed experiment

n_cpp, n_wc, n_kpp, n_gpp = (int(cc.get(c, 0)) for c in ("CPP", "WC-CPP", "KPP", "GPP"))
assert n_cpp + n_wc + n_kpp + n_gpp == n_par
n_crit = n_cpp + n_wc
cls_txt = join_and([f"{n} {c}" + ("s" if n != 1 else "") for c, n in

# every NOR in force lies within the characterized range of its parameter
for k in steps:

# --- set-points and NORs changed at Version 2.0 by the report of their step -------------
def _lc(s):
    return s if s[:2].isupper() else s[0].lower() + s[1:]

def _phrase(name, nc, spm):
    n = _lc(name)
    if nc == "moved" and spm:
        return f"the NOR and the set-point of {n} were moved"
    if nc and spm:
        return f"the NOR of {n} was {nc} and its set-point moved"
    if nc:
        return f"the NOR of {n} was {nc}"
    return f"the set-point of {n} was moved"

def _serial(xs):
    if len(xs) == 1:
        return xs[0]
    if len(xs) == 2:
        return f"{xs[0]} and {xs[1]}"
    return ", ".join(xs[:-1]) + ", and " + xs[-1]

        if nc or spm:

quant = (meth[~meth["id"].isin(titre["id"])]

assert quant.loc[0, "id"] == "AMV-3014"                     # the residual DNA qPCR is the least precise
least_prec = quant.loc[0, "precision_pct"]
hcp_rank = int(quant.index[quant["id"] == "AMV-3012"][0]) + 1
hcp_prec = quant.loc[hcp_rank - 1, "precision_pct"]
hcp_rank_txt = {1: "the least precise", 2: "the second least precise",
                3: "the third least precise"}[hcp_rank]
assert "AMV-3020" not in set(meth["id"])                    # no record of nrCE-SDS performance here
for _id in ("AMV-3013", "AMV-3014", "AMV-3021"):
    assert _id in set(meth["id"])
meth_frame = pd.DataFrame({
    "Reference": meth["id"],
    "Analytical method": meth["name"],
    "Intermediate precision": meth["precision_pct"].map(lambda v: f"{v:g}"),
    "Limit of quantitation": [f"{a:g} {u}" for a, u in zip(meth["loq"], meth["loq_unit"])],
    "Accuracy (%)": meth["accuracy_pct"].map(lambda v: f"{v:g}"),
})
tbl_meth = T.frame(

    align=["l", "P{6.0cm}", "c", "P{3.4cm}", "c"],
    notes=[("", "Intermediate precision is a relative standard deviation in percent. For the infectivity "
                f"titre assays ({join_and(titre['id'].tolist())}) it is a standard deviation in log10 units, "
                "the form that the viral clearance calculation uses.")])

# the host cell protein ELISA supports the criteria of all three chromatography steps

assert set(iac.loc[iac["cqa"] == "hcp", "step_key"]) == {"protein_a", "cex", "aex"}

# --- scale-down models and viral clearance ----------------------------------------------
offset_ci = int(round(100 * float(CFG.raw()["analytics"]["sdm"]["offset_ci"])))
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

This plan governs the transfer of the `{python} PRODUCT` drug substance manufacturing process from the development site of `{python} COMPANY` in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION` to its commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`. The transfer covers the manufacturing process, the analytical methods that test the intermediates and the drug substance, and the control strategy that connects them. @sec-product describes the process, and @sec-sites names the work that each site holds.

This plan is the parent document of the `{python} PRODUCT` process characterization package. The package has `{python} n_docs` documents, including this plan, and @tbl-package lists the others. The risk assessment RA-001 sets the scope of each study. Each Process Characterization Plan (PCP-003 to PCP-010) commits a study, and each paired Process Characterization Report (PCR-003 to PCR-010) records what that study found. The master plan PCMP-001 sets the framework that the step plans apply, and the master report PCMR-001 consolidates the reports. Together these documents justify the operating ranges and the control strategy that the receiving site will run. The package also holds two investigation reports of Quality Assurance. The investigation `{python} inv_id` is the reason for this revision (@sec-changes), and the investigation `{python} inv2_id` concerns the adequacy of the response-surface models in the step reports. A reader who wants the risk basis of the study scope should start at RA-001. A reader who wants the consolidated outcome should start at PCMR-001.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(corpus_docs_md(DOC))
print()
print(": The other documents of the A-Mab characterization package. {#tbl-package}")
```

Three activities are outside the scope of this plan. Drug product manufacture, filling and finishing are transferred under a separate plan. Cell bank manufacture and testing are governed by their own records. The execution of the process performance qualification (PPQ) campaign is also outside this plan. This plan sets the conditions the campaign must meet before it may start and the strategy it will follow (@sec-ppq). The campaign will be executed under its own protocol and reported separately.

The transfer follows ICH Q10, which places technology transfer within the pharmaceutical quality system [@ichq10], and the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011]. In that lifecycle, process characterization is Stage 1 (process design) and process performance qualification is Stage 2. The enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 and ICH Q11 governs how the design space and the control strategy are defined [@ichq8; @ichq11]. ICH Q9 governs the risk assessment that scopes the studies [@ichq9], and ICH Q5A governs the evaluation of viral safety [@ichq5a]. The process model, the quality attribute framework and the risk method follow the published A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} appr_v1`, before the risk assessment RA-001 (`{python} ra_appr`), the master plan PCMP-001 (`{python} pcmp_appr`) and the first characterization study, `{python} first_study`, which started on `{python} first_start`. Version 2.0 replaces it under corrective action CA3 of the QA investigation `{python} inv_id`. Quality Assurance opened the investigation on `{python} inv_opened`, after its review of PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for BLA readiness, and closed it on `{python} inv_closed` with the classification `{python} inv_class`. The investigation found that the criteria used to judge each step in the proven acceptable range (PAR) analysis had been set after the data were seen and were in no approved protocol (`{python} inv_id` finding 1). This plan set no step criteria. This revision makes the following changes:

1. The title block of Version 1.0 carried `{python} pkg_date`, the date on which the Version 1.0 package was compiled, in place of the date on which this plan was approved (`{python} inv_id` finding 5). The revision history now gives the approval date. @sec-schedule records the approval date of each step plan and the execution window of the studies recorded in the Version 1.0 reports (@tbl-chronology).
2. Where this plan states what an intermediate is judged against, it now refers to the intermediate acceptance criteria of the master plan PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.3. This applies to the comparison of the sites (@sec-sdm), the control strategy (@sec-control) and the qualification campaign (@sec-ppq). These criteria are derived a priori from the drug substance criteria and the platform worst case of each downstream step. Version 1.0 referred to the limit that each characterization report would establish for its own step. Limits set in that way were the subject of `{python} inv_id` findings 1 and 2. The viral clearance claims of the three claimed steps now refer to PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.4.
3. Where this plan describes the qualification of the scale-down models (@sec-equivalency, @sec-sdm and @sec-gaps), it now refers to the offset rule of PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.1. A model is qualified for each output by its offset from manufacturing scale, not by a test of equivalence, and every judgement against a criterion is stated at manufacturing scale.
4. The quality attributes in @tbl-cqa now include fragments (low molecular weight species), with a criterion measured by non-reduced capillary electrophoresis with sodium dodecyl sulfate (nrCE-SDS). The CQA register assigns fragments to harvest, where they form during the harvest hold. The description of harvest in @tbl-train and the basis on which the harvest gap is accepted (@sec-gaps) are restated for this reason. Following the analytical method decision `{python} amd_id` of `{python} amd_date`, nrCE-SDS (SOP-3015, AMV-3020) is added to the methods to transfer (@sec-methods). The decision answers `{python} inv_id` finding 6, that size exclusion chromatography (SEC) reads fragments high in samples that still carry host cell protein. @tbl-methods-by-study shows which method measured fragments in which designed study.

The procedures and method validations in @tbl-sops now also include the product titre method by Protein A affinity HPLC (SOP-3016, AMV-3021). @tbl-methods gives the qualified performance of every method in the method record. Beside the methods of the Version 1.0 table, it now includes the charge variant method by icIEF (AMV-3013), the residual DNA method by qPCR (AMV-3014) and the product titre method (AMV-3021).

# Product and process description {#sec-product}

`{python} PRODUCT` is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody. Its primary mechanism of action is antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). The fucose and galactose content of its N-linked glycan therefore affects efficacy, and both are quality attributes of the drug substance. The glycan is formed in the production bioreactor. None of the platform purification steps separates glycosylation variants under the conditions used here [@amab2009]. Protein A binds the Fc region at the interface of the CH2 and CH3 domains. The glycan takes no part in that binding, so Protein A captures every glycan variant alike. Fucose, galactose and mannose carry no charge, so the two ion exchange steps, which separate by charge, do not resolve these variants either. Control of the glycan attributes therefore sits in cell culture. For this reason the transfer of the cell culture step carries more risk to product quality than the transfer of any single purification step.

The drug substance is made at a production bioreactor working volume of `{python} f"{scale_l:,}"` L. It leaves the final formulation step at a target concentration of `{python} ds_conc` g/L. The train has `{python} n_steps` unit operations, numbered Step `{python} step_first` to Step `{python} step_last`. @tbl-train lists them with the principal role of each in the control strategy.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(md_table(["Step", "Unit operation", "Principal role"], train_rows, [8, 30, 62]))
print()
print(": The A-Mab drug substance process train and the principal role of each step. {#tbl-train}")
```

The purification sequence is the platform sequence of the earlier humanized IgG1 products of `{python} COMPANY`, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. Capture on Protein A is followed by a low-pH hold, cation exchange, anion exchange, small virus retentive filtration, and ultrafiltration with diafiltration (UF/DF). The low-pH hold, the anion exchange step and the virus filter each carry a viral clearance claim. The three claims are modular in the sense of ICH Q5A [@ichq5a]. Each step is studied and claimed on its own, and no single step report claims the cumulative clearance of the train. The master report PCMR-001 states the cumulative clearance.

@tbl-cqa lists the `{python} n_cqa` quality attributes that the transfer must preserve, with the acceptance criterion and the criticality of each. Criticality is a continuum, not a binary split into critical and non-critical, as in the case study [@amab2009] and the risk principles of ICH Q9 [@ichq9]. The attributes ranked high and very high drive the scope of the studies.

Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose depend on how far the cell processes the glycan in the Golgi. That processing changes with the nutrient supply and with the dissolved gas concentrations in the bioreactor. Acidic charge variants accumulate through the deamidation of asparagine residues. The rate of deamidation rises with pH and temperature, and the extent rises with the time the product spends at those conditions. Aggregate forms in the culture. Cation exchange reduces it, because the resin binds the high molecular weight species more strongly than the monomer, and these species stay on the column when the pool is cut. Fragments form in culture and during the harvest hold, where proteases released from lysed cells clip the antibody. The CQA register therefore assigns them to harvest. Host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are removed by the chromatography steps. Each of these steps either binds the impurity while the antibody flows past or elutes the antibody away from it. The two viral clearance requirements are cumulative. The register assigns each to one step, but each requirement is met by the sum of the claims of several steps.

```{python}
#| output: asis
tbl_cqa.show()
```

# Sending and receiving sites {#sec-sites}

The sending site is the development site of `{python} COMPANY` in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION`. The receiving site is the commercial drug substance site of `{python} COMPANY` in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`. Both sites belong to the same sponsor and work under one pharmaceutical quality system and one change control procedure. ICH Q10 places technology transfer within that quality system [@ichq10]. A change to a set-point, a range or an analytical method during the transfer is therefore assessed once and applied at both sites.

The development site keeps the qualified scale-down models, the execution and the statistical analysis of the characterization studies, and the authorship of the characterization plans and reports. It also keeps the process description and the justification of the operating ranges until those are approved. The receiving site takes ownership of commercial manufacture. That ownership covers the master batch record, the operation of the equipment train at commercial scale, the engineering and qualification batches, and the routine testing that supports batch release.

The division between the sites is one of work, not of accountability. Both sites review and approve the process description, and Quality Assurance at both sites approves each handover listed in @sec-schedule. Where a characterization study supports a range that the receiving site cannot hold, the two sites resolve it together before the range is written into a batch record.

# Site equivalency analysis {#sec-equivalency}

Equivalency was assessed for each element that can carry a process difference between the two sites. @tbl-equivalency gives the assessment. The assessment is prospective. Each row therefore states what is compared and how a difference is managed, not a measured outcome.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(md_table(["Element", "Sending site", "Receiving site", "How the difference is managed"],
               equiv_rows, [17, 22, 24, 37]))
print()
print(": Site equivalency assessment for the elements that can carry a process difference. {#tbl-equivalency}")
```

The largest difference between the sites is scale. The receiving site runs the production bioreactor at `{python} f"{scale_l:,}"` L, while the characterization studies run at the scale-down volumes qualified under SOP-1001 (Qualification of Scale-Down Models). In cell culture, scale acts through mixing and through gas transfer. At constant power per unit volume, mixing time rises with vessel volume. A bolus of feed therefore takes longer to disperse, and cells near the addition point spend longer at a high local concentration. Carbon dioxide is stripped less efficiently as the liquid column deepens, because a sparge bubble that rises through more liquid comes closer to equilibrium with the culture before it leaves. Oxygen crosses the same interface in the other direction, from the bubble into the culture. A change in the gas path therefore does not change the two transfers equally. Oxygen supply and carbon dioxide removal are matched separately when a bioreactor model is qualified.

In the purification steps, scale acts through column packing and through pressure. A chromatography column is scaled by holding the bed height and the linear velocity constant. This keeps the residence time of the mobile phase, but not the wall support that stabilizes a narrow bed. A wide commercial column can therefore lose plate count at a pressure drop that the model tolerates. A filter is scaled by area at constant flux, which holds the transmembrane pressure only while the feed carries the same load of particles. @sec-sdm describes how a model is qualified against these differences.

The second difference is process control. Automated control at the receiving site holds a parameter closer to its set-point than manual control does, and so narrows the distribution that the commercial process will deliver. A narrower distribution does not invalidate a range, because every NOR lies within the characterized range of its parameter (@tbl-parameters-by-step). The reverse case matters more. Where the receiving site cannot hold a parameter inside the NOR that the characterization assumes, either the range must be widened by further study or the equipment must be changed.

The remaining elements in @tbl-equivalency carry a difference in documentation, not in the process. Buffer preparation is the one element in that group that still needs a study, because central preparation adds a hold before use that laboratory preparation does not have. That study belongs to the receiving site and is listed in @sec-gaps.

# Scale-down model and comparability strategy {#sec-sdm}

The characterization studies do not run at commercial scale. They run on scale-down models, and every conclusion drawn from them reaches the commercial process through the qualification of those models. Qualification is performed under SOP-1001 (Qualification of Scale-Down Models). The lifecycle guidance expects a manufacturer to understand how far a laboratory model represents the commercial process [@fda2011].

A model is set up in two parts. Parameters that do not depend on scale, such as pH, temperature and dissolved oxygen, are run at the values proposed for commercial manufacture. Parameters that depend on scale, such as agitation, gas flow, bed height, linear velocity and filtration flux, are set so that the model reproduces the performance of the commercial train. Its dimensions need not match. For the chromatography steps the model keeps the bed height and the residence time of the manufacturing column, and column efficiency is checked by plate count and peak asymmetry. For the production bioreactor, agitation and gas flow are set to match the oxygen transfer and the carbon dioxide stripping of the commercial vessel.

Each model is qualified for each output separately, by the offset rule of the master plan PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.1. The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs at set-point minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches, with its two-sided `{python} offset_ci` % confidence interval. A model may differ in mean from manufacturing scale, provided the offset is known precisely enough. For an output compared at both scales, every judgement of a scale-down result against a criterion therefore subtracts the offset first, so ranges and conclusions are stated at manufacturing scale. A model is qualified for an output when the conclusion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its interval.

The qualification runs are made, and the offset of each output is estimated, before the first characterization run of the step. For a step with a response-surface design, the decision whether the model is qualified for an output is made at analysis, because the conclusion over the NOR comes from that model. The qualification does not compare fragments or viral clearance at both scales. Their offset is unknown, not zero. Their representativeness rests on the mechanism of the step for fragments and on the spiking model for viral clearance (PCMP-001 §7.1).

@tbl-scope gives the scope of the characterization. For each unit operation it lists the number of parameters in scope, how they divide between multivariate and univariate study, and the plan and report that cover the step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(md_table(["Step", "Unit operation", "Parameters", "Multivariate", "Univariate", "Documents"],
               scope_rows, [7, 33, 13, 14, 13, 20]))
print()
print(": Characterization scope per unit operation and the documents that cover it. {#tbl-scope}")
```

Across the train, `{python} n_par` parameters are in scope. Of these, `{python} n_mv` are studied in multivariate designs and `{python} n_uv` one factor at a time. RA-001 assigned no parameter of harvest (Step `{python} s_har`) or UF/DF (Step `{python} s_ufdf`) to multivariate study, so neither step carries a designed experiment. Their ranges rest on univariate work and on platform experience, and no interaction between two of their parameters is estimated (@sec-gaps).

Comparability between the two sites is demonstrated on material, not on documents. The receiving site will run engineering batches on the commercial train before the qualification campaign starts. Each batch will be sampled at every step and tested by the transferred methods. The drug substance from these batches will be compared with the acceptance criteria in @tbl-cqa. Each intermediate will be compared with its intermediate acceptance criterion from PCMP-001 §7.3, where one is defined.

Comparability is judged against these criteria and not against the means observed in development. A development mean is a property of the scale-down model and of the few batches behind it. Under the offset rule a scale-down mean may differ from the manufacturing mean, so a commercial batch that differs from a development mean does not thereby differ in quality. Prior knowledge from the earlier humanized IgG1 products supports the expectation that the platform purification steps behave the same way at both scales [@amab2009]. However, the engineering batches confirm that expectation. It is not assumed from the platform.

## The analytical methods {#sec-methods}

The methods in scope are the release and characterization methods for the drug substance and the in-process methods that support the control of the intermediates. @tbl-methods lists the `{python} n_meth` methods in the method record, with the performance each demonstrated at qualification.

```{python}
#| output: asis
tbl_meth.show()
```

Among the quantitative methods in @tbl-methods, the residual DNA method by qPCR (AMV-3014) is the least precise, at `{python} f"{least_prec:g}"` %. The host cell protein ELISA (AMV-3012) is `{python} hcp_rank_txt`, at `{python} f"{hcp_prec:g}"` %. It supports the host cell protein clearance argument across all three chromatography steps, and every judgement of host cell protein against an intermediate acceptance criterion rests on its results. Its transfer should therefore be completed and reviewed before the engineering batches are run.

The product titre method by Protein A affinity HPLC (AMV-3021, under SOP-3016) measures the antibody in the clarified harvest. The protein load of the Protein A step is set from that result. Protein concentration by A280 (AMV-3019) counts every protein in a clarified harvest, not the antibody alone, and so cannot set the load.

From `{python} amd_date`, fragments are measured by nrCE-SDS (AMV-3020, under SOP-3015) in every study at every step. This follows the analytical method decision `{python} amd_id` (PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.8). The decision followed the method comparability study S-CEX-FRC, in which SEC and nrCE-SDS were run on the same samples. SEC read fragments high wherever the sample still carried host cell protein, because part of the host cell protein elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC (`{python} inv_id` finding 6). SEC remains the method for aggregate, where no such interference applies. The receiving site therefore needs nrCE-SDS for fragments and SEC for aggregate. The nrCE-SDS method is transferred and requalified in the same way as every method in @tbl-methods. Its qualified performance is recorded in AMV-3020 and is not part of the method record in @tbl-methods, so the transfer protocol takes the values to be reproduced from AMV-3020.

@tbl-methods-by-study shows which method measured aggregate and fragments in each designed study. Designs run before the decision measured fragments by SEC. The retained response-surface samples of Protein A and low-pH viral inactivation were re-tested by nrCE-SDS, and the cation exchange response-surface design measured fragments by both methods on every run. Where the characterization reports base a decision on fragments, they use nrCE-SDS results.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study().show()
```

Each method will be transferred under a written protocol and requalified at the receiving site before it is used to test comparability material. A transfer is successful when the receiving site reproduces the qualified intermediate precision of the method and returns accuracy within the qualified range on a common set of samples. If the receiving site cannot meet the qualified precision, the cause should be investigated and corrected before the exercise is repeated. A method may not be used for in-process or release testing until its transfer has passed.

Analytical Development at the sending site owns the transfer protocols and the comparison of the two data sets. Quality Control at the receiving site executes the transfers. Quality Assurance approves the outcome. The person who executes a method transfer may not approve it.

## The control strategy {#sec-control}

The control strategy is the set of controls that together assure the quality of the drug substance. In this transfer it has three layers. Parameter classification places every process parameter in a class and attaches a control to it. In-process limits bound what each intermediate may deliver to the next step. Release testing confirms the attributes of the drug substance against @tbl-cqa.

Classification is performed under SOP-4001 on the evidence of the characterization studies. Each report classifies the parameters of its own step, and the master report PCMR-001 consolidates the classification for the whole train. A parameter whose variability affects a quality attribute is a critical process parameter (CPP). It is a well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP) where the risk of leaving the design space is low. A parameter that affects process consistency without affecting quality is a key process parameter (KPP). The remaining parameters are general process parameters (GPPs), which the batch record controls without a claim of criticality [@amab2009]. At this revision the train has `{python} cls_txt` (@tbl-parameters-by-step).

In the characterization, each step output on which a drug substance criterion depends is judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion (PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.3). The criterion is the drug substance criterion carried backward through the train, using the worst case that each downstream step showed on the platform products X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. No margin is applied. The derivation uses no data from the studies it judges. Each step report checks the platform worst cases of its own step, and PCMP-001 §7.5 states when that check tightens or widens a criterion upstream. The master plan gives `{python} n_iac` such criteria across `{python} n_iac_steps` steps.

Viral safety rests on three independent steps, not on any one of them. The low-pH hold inactivates enveloped virus. The anion exchange step removes both enveloped and small virus in flow-through mode, and the virus filter removes small virus by size. Inactivation by pH, removal by charge and removal by size act on different properties of the virus particle. A particle that survives one step is therefore no more likely to survive the next, and the log reductions are added [@ichq5a]. Each claimed step is held to its platform claim (PCMP-001 §7.4). For XMuLV the claims sum to `{python} f"{x_sum:g}"` log10 against a cumulative requirement of `{python} f"{x_req:g}"`. For MVM they sum to `{python} f"{m_sum:g}"` against `{python} f"{m_req:g}"`. The load conditions on which each claim depends, such as the pH and the conductivity of the anion exchange load, are controlled by the batch record. PCMR-001 states the cumulative clearance and compares it with the acceptance criteria in @tbl-cqa.

The control strategy is transferred when PCMR-001 has been approved and the classes it consolidates have been written into the master batch record. Until then the receiving site works to the ranges in the current process description. That basis is suitable for engineering batches. It is not sufficient for qualification batches.

# Process performance qualification strategy {#sec-ppq}

Process performance qualification is the Stage 2 activity that follows this transfer [@fda2011]. It demonstrates that the commercial process, run by the receiving site with the transferred methods and control strategy, reproducibly delivers drug substance of the required quality. This plan does not execute that demonstration. It states what must be in place before the campaign may start and the strategy the campaign will follow.

The campaign will manufacture `{python} n_ppq` consecutive batches at commercial scale under the approved master batch record. Every parameter will be held at its set-point in @tbl-parameters-by-step, and no deliberate excursion will be run. The campaign will not challenge the edges of the characterized ranges. Those edges are established at small scale, and a qualification batch is not a characterization experiment. However, a campaign of this size cannot capture the variability that commercial manufacture will show over its life.

The campaign may start when the following conditions are met:

1. The characterization package is complete and PCMR-001 has been approved.
2. Every method used for in-process and release testing has been transferred and requalified at the receiving site.
3. The commercial equipment train and the utilities that serve it are qualified.
4. The master batch record carries the confirmed set-points, the confirmed ranges and the in-process controls.
5. The gaps in @sec-gaps are closed, or Quality Assurance has assessed and accepted in writing the residual risk of an open gap.

Sampling during the campaign will follow the sampling plans of the step plans. Each intermediate is then tested against the same intermediate acceptance criterion as in the characterization (PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.3). The acceptance criteria of the campaign will be stated in the qualification protocol. The master plan PCMP-001 plans the characterization campaign that produces the evidence, and the master report PCMR-001 consolidates it. Both are approved before the qualification campaign starts.

Continued process verification begins when the qualification campaign is complete. The receiving site will draft the monitoring plan during the campaign. The plan may not be finalized until the campaign data are available, because its control limits are derived from the performance that the commercial process actually shows [@fda2011].

# Gap analysis {#sec-gaps}

The gaps were identified at the approval of Version 1.0 of this plan, by comparing what the receiving site held with what the qualification campaign requires. @tbl-gaps lists each gap with its impact, the action that closes it and the function that owns the action. A gap must be closed before the qualification campaign starts, or its residual risk must be assessed and accepted under the quality system [@ichq9].

The first two gaps set the schedule. Each needs laboratory work at a site that has not yet done it, and neither can be closed by a review of documents. The remaining gaps are closed by sequencing, by training or by a bounded qualification study, and none of them needs a change to the process itself.

The gap on harvest and UF/DF will still be open when the characterization campaign ends, because no multivariate design is planned for either step at any point in the programme. It is accepted for the reason that the risk assessment RA-001 assigned the parameters of both steps to univariate study. None of them was ranked high, and none was expected to interact with another parameter (PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §4). An interaction between two of them is therefore not expected to move a result in @tbl-cqa.
